text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Officials in Washington said the United States was preparing for a new initiative in the Middle East peace process after the start of Clinton's second term on January 20. They said Clinton had decided to invite Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, King Hussein of Jordan and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to visit the United States, probably in February, to decide the next steps in the process.

- Damascus Declaration foreign ministers will start their 14th meeting at the Egyptian foreign ministry on Saturday evening. They will discuss developments in the peace process, economic, political and security cooperation and Iranian-Arab relations.
- Presidential adviser Osama el-Baz said a project for an Arab common market is being drawn up, based on gradual steps.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa called on states in the region, including Iran, to refrain from any action likely to raise problems and tension in the region.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid announced that the privatisation programme for 1997 envisages the sale of 11 companies through the stock exchange and new incentives for the sale of 40 companies in full to main investors. The incentives include abolition of the maximum stake individuals may buy and allowing a single investor to own 20 percent of a company initially, subject to increase later.
- Voice of Palestine radio said Palestinian planning minister Nabil Shaath will bring a letter from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to President Mubarak today.

- Sudanese opposition leader Sadeq al-Mahdi arrived in Cairo, saying he is asking for Egypt's help to save the people of Sudan. He said that Hassan al-Turabi and his party imposed themselves by force and distorted the image of Islam.
- President Mubarak will meet the Damascus Declaration foreign ministers.
- Shipping in the Suez Canal was held up yesterday because a Chinese cargo vessel lost electrical power. Four tugs towed the vessel to Suez roads.
- The ruling National Democratic Party will nominate its candidates for local council elections within days.
- President Mubarak met investors in the Red Sea resort of Hurghada yesterday.
- Atef Obeid said 35 troubled or loss-making public-sector companies would be restructured by June. Their factories will not be sold to investors as scrap or cheaply, he added.

- Ahmed el-Sayyed, chairman of the state's National Company for Contsriction and Devevlopment, said the state would sell more shares in Heliopolis Housing and Development, Shams Housing and Development and Maadi Housing and Development.
- A member of parliament and 11 local councillors, all from the opposition Labour party, were among the leaders of the new Moslem Brotherhood organisation which the police uncovered on Thursday.
